minor.issue: Soft-deleted valuations (deleted_at set) are STILL retrievable via GET /valuations/{vid} — only the LIST endpoint filters out deleted_at. Not user-visible because the UI only surfaces via list, but the API is asymmetric. Consider adding {'deleted_at': {'$exists': False}} to the get_valuation Mongo query, or return 404 for soft-deleted rows.

action_items: Optional: symmetric soft-delete on GET /valuations/{vid} (add deleted_at exists filter or return 404).

Nit: valuation_workbench.py needs PYTHONPATH=/app/backend when running unit-test file from /app root; conftest.py already sets it inside /app/backend so 'cd /app/backend && pytest' works — main agent can add sys.path handling to unit test or leave a README note.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /valuations/{vid} is soft-delete but GET /valuations/{vid} does not filter deleted_at, so the resource remains fetchable indefinitely by id. Low-severity but asymmetric.

ValuationsList.jsx list card renders v.aggregate.low_usd/high_usd formatted with fmtUsd but if aggregate exists with base_usd but null low/high they render as em-dash — acceptable; watch out for autofill result that sets base_usd without band bounds (didn't repro but math paths in aggregate_band should guarantee low/high).

ValuationWorkbench.jsx polls autofill_status every 3s but never enforces a max-attempts / timeout — if the backend hangs indefinitely the poll will run until page unload. Consider capping at ~40 polls (2 min) and rendering a 'Taking longer than usual' state.
Confidence pill: aggregate.confidence 'low' maps to pill-amber (visual conflict with pending/failed pills also using amber). Consider a distinct 'pill-red' for 'low' vs banner amber.
downloadPdf in ValuationWorkbench.jsx uses fetch + Bearer header (correct for auth). No progress state — for large PDFs users might click twice; add a per-snapshot 'downloading…' state on the button.

rca of the issue: No blocking bug. One low-severity asymmetry: DELETE is soft-delete (sets deleted_at) and LIST filters by deleted_at, but GET /valuations/{vid} does not filter, so a deleted valuation is still retrievable by id. Reproduce: POST /valuations, DELETE it, then GET /valuations/{that_id} → returns 200 with the doc (including deleted_at). Mitigation: add `'deleted_at': {'$exists': False}` to the query in get_valuation (server.py:3112) or return 404 when deleted_at is set. The associated snapshot + PDF endpoints have the same asymmetry inherited from the parent doc lookup.
